clue.text: Tired as a carpet no longer fashionable

parts.note: a shag carpet has a long, rough pile, so a carpet can be described as shagged
something out of fashion is out

explanation.surface: Worn down like a carpet that has gone out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: Shag-pile carpet was a 1970s fashion, so the surface is a dated carpet; shagged out is crude British slang for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Shagged out is British slang meaning utterly exhausted, worn out.

clue.text: Getting the collywobbles, key NI politician trades one for an E

parts.note: A is a musical key

indicators.note: trading means swapping one item away, so a letter in the politician's name is exchanged
in exchange for: names the incoming piece that takes the place of the one traded away

parts.note: David Trimble led the Ulster Unionists and was First Minister of Northern Ireland
the Roman numeral for one
the letter E itself, the clue naming it outright

explanation.surface: A leading Northern Ireland politician gets nervous and swaps something for an ecstasy pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E' suggests ecstasy; it is only the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Atremble means trembling, which is how someone with the collywobbles, a fit of nerves, would be.

clue.text: Despicable type, one of ten joining Sun, say

parts.note: people have ten toes
The Sun is one example of a rag, a scornful word for a tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A contemptible figure joins the Sun newspaper as one of its ten new hires.
explanation.definitionFit: A toerag is British slang for a worthless, contemptible person.

clue.text: Caught unawares "making a contribution to" Lamont, he hoped

indicators.note: the answer contributes letters to the words that follow, so it lies inside them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Norman Lamont, the Chancellor, was hoping someone would pay into his funds and was taken by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around the indicator hint that it is a device, not a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch someone on the hop is a British idiom meaning to take them by surprise.

clue.text: Tatty rag much used by drivers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Daily ..., a British tabloid newspaper that Private Eye mocks
second meaning: the glass a driver checks to see behind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag' looks like a cloth used for wiping a car, but it is a scornful word for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror lets a motorist see traffic behind, and the Mirror is a well-known British tabloid.

clue.text: PC name for Blair's number two in school

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the word for school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: second, so only the second letter of Blair's is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The correct term for Tony Blair's deputy at school, or a crude joke about his toilet habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number two' looks like Blair's deputy or a toilet joke; it is the position of a letter. PC Plod is the policeman in the Noddy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Plod is a British slang word for the police, after PC Plod in Enid Blyton's stories.

clue.text: This wobbly behind does one's head in — stupid

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and out of shape, so the four letters of This are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
to be behind a cause is to be for it, in favour of it
to brain someone is to strike them on the head, so the clue's phrase stands for that verb

explanation.surface: A wobbling backside that drives you mad, dismissed as plain idiocy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a noun for the backside, which the wobbly surface invites; it is the preposition sense, supporting. The phrase is a single noun used here as an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A shit-for-brains is a coarse British insult for a very foolish person, so the phrase stands for stupidity.

clue.text: Harry inserts rounded file in the butt

indicators.note: Harry, the whole answer, has these letters put into its outer part, so this signals an insertion
places the reworked letters inside the word standing for the butt

parts.note: a butt is the thick end of something, as in a cigarette butt

indicators.note: rounded off or reshaped, so the letters of file are reworked rather than kept in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Harry is jamming a smooth file into a backside, a typical piece of Private Eye smut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a verb (to harass) or the prince, but it is the first name of the comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Enfield is the British comedian, so his first name serves as a by-name definition of his surname.

clue.text: Look round before getting leg over

parts.note: a round shape is the letter that looks like a circle

indicators.note: knocked over, so the letters of leg are tumbled into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Eyeing someone up before getting a bit of how's-your-father, 'leg over' being British slang for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg over' reads as one slang phrase, but the two words split into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look at someone lecherously, a stronger synonym for look.

clue.text: Queen's rather common consort? Unhealthy occupation

parts.note: feeling rough is British for feeling ill
a trade is a line of work

explanation.surface: A dig at the Queen's husband being low-class, and a remark about a job that is bad for you.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is slang for a gay man, not the monarch; rough trade is gay slang for a working-class casual partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough trade means a rough, working-class sexual partner, which is a common consort for a gay man.

clue.text: The art of being on top, having sex with another bloke's cool

definitions.text: The art of being on top

parts.note: being up someone is crude British slang for having sex with them
a bloke is a man, so another bloke's is a man's
hip means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: Dominance as a technique, achieved by sleeping with another man's partner, which looks cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On top' suggests a sexual position, but the definition means getting the better of others.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmanship, also called one-upmanship, is the skill of keeping an advantage over other people.

clue.text: Where you shut your eyes to FBI surveillance? Sucker!

parts.note: bed is where you close your eyes to sleep
a bug is a hidden listening device, used in surveillance

explanation.surface: Somewhere you close your eyes to being spied on by the FBI, and you are a mug for doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a jeer at the person being bugged; it is a creature that sucks blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedbugs are insects that feed on human blood, so they are literally suckers.

clue.text: Prince: ""Mater has not quite finished tipping glass of piss over one"

parts.note: mater is old public-school slang for mother, ma

indicators.note: the word has stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: taken as written, before being cut

indicators.note: a glass tipped up is turned over, so the word for it is read backwards

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer, and piss is slang for weak beer

explanation.surface: A prince tells how his mother, still drinking, upends a pint of lager over someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja is an Indian ruling prince, the great king of a princely state.

clue.text: One on the lookout for dirt, note, goes round dodgy urinals

definitions.text: One on the lookout for dirt

indicators.note: the word for note surrounds the rest

parts.note: to jot is to note something down; a jot is also a tiny amount

indicators.note: suspect and unreliable, so the letters of urinals are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grubby figure peering around public toilets for something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirt' reads as grime in the toilets, but it means scandal, gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist, especially a tabloid one, hunts for scandal and gossip, which is dirt in this sense.

clue.text: Prick gives up drug, has an E, another name for the drug

indicators.note: giving something up means losing it, so a letter standing for the drug is removed

parts.note: prick and cock are both vulgar slang for the penis
C is a common abbreviation for cocaine
taken as the letter E

explanation.surface: An idiot quits one drug, drops an ecstasy pill instead, and talks of street names for drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E' looks like an ecstasy tablet; it is just the letter added.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is the usual slang name for cocaine, the drug referred to earlier.

clue.text: Peg riding a Page 3 girl?

parts.note: a pin is a peg used to fasten things
a rider on a horse is up, as racing commentators say

explanation.surface: A girl from the tabloid's Page 3 riding a peg, a ludicrous picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 of the British Sun newspaper used to carry a photo of a topless model.
explanation.definitionFit: A Page 3 girl is an example of a pin-up, a glamour model whose picture people stick on walls.

clue.text: Senior pisspoor in the art of spin — timeserver

indicators.note: the reworked letters go inside the abbreviation for the art of spin

parts.note: PR is public relations, the business of spin

indicators.note: something piss-poor is a mess, so the letters of senior are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior figure who is hopeless at spin doctoring, merely serving out his time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeserver' usually means someone coasting in a job; here it is one serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner is someone serving time in jail, so this is a witty use of timeserver.

clue.text: Corporations backing filth

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for corporations is read in reverse

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a fat belly, a tum

explanation.surface: Big businesses giving money to support pornography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporations' looks like companies, but it is the old humorous word for paunches.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is obscene, dirty material, so it is a synonym for filth.

clue.text: Viewers intent on taking in Kirsty's top, exposed

indicators.note: taking something in means enclosing it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: starers are viewers fixed on something

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gawping onlookers ogling Kirsty's topless pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as a garment Kirsty has removed; it is the first letter of her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is British slang for stark naked, completely exposed.

clue.text: Celeb stalked by Ray, possibly a crawler in the main

indicators.note: someone being stalked has the stalker following behind, so the second piece comes after

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a ray is one example of a fish

explanation.surface: A celebrity is followed by a man named Ray, perhaps a creep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name, the stalker; it is the flat sea creature. The main is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A starfish creeps slowly along the seabed, so it is a crawler living in the ocean.

clue.text: The very latest he'd jiggled balls outside

indicators.note: the word for balls sits outside, around the rearranged letters

parts.note: balls and rot are both slang for nonsense

indicators.note: shaken about, so the letters of he'd are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man fondling his testicles, and it is the hottest news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' looks anatomical, but here it means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-hot news is the newest and most exciting, so the phrase means up to the minute.

clue.text: See 7
Act like rabbits and go in for frottage up on the range

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run from bottom to top, in reverse

parts.note: frottage is sexual rubbing, so to go in for it is to rub
a row is a line, like a mountain range

explanation.surface: Mating like rabbits and rubbing against each other in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act like rabbits' suggests constant sex; it means digging a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbits burrow, digging underground tunnels, so to burrow is to behave like a rabbit.

clue.text: Dick penetrated by old, excited peasant

indicators.note: something penetrated has another thing pushed into it, so the reworked letters go inside

parts.note: both dick and chopper are slang for the penis

indicators.note: stirred up, so the three letters of old are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sex scene between an aged, aroused man and a country labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy rustic, a disparaging term for a farm labourer.

clue.text: Connect live one to end of Jonathan King

parts.note: L marks the live terminal on a British three-pin plug

indicators.note: the final letter of Jonathan

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Linking a live wire to the end of the disgraced pop impresario Jonathan King.
explanation.definitionFit: To link two things is to join or connect them.

clue.text: Kay takes off top

parts.note: the letter K is spelt out as kay
feeling off means feeling ill

explanation.surface: Someone called Kay removes her top.
explanation.walkthrough: Kay looks like a name, but it is how the letter K is spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for to murder them, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Tories failed to get this popular energy

parts.note: being in is being fashionable, popular
power is energy in physics and engineering

explanation.surface: The Conservatives lost the election because they lacked any popular vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: When this was set, Labour had won elections and the Conservatives had not been able to form a government.
explanation.definitionFit: A party that loses the election does not win office, so the Tories missed out on government.

clue.text: Rude and clumsy Johnson squeezes ball, hard

indicators.note: something squeezed in sits tight inside, so the ball letter goes inside the name

parts.note: Boris Johnson, the politician
a ball has the round shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A sly comment on Boris Johnson's famously awkward manner and fumbling with a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Boorish means behaving like a boor, someone coarse and ill-mannered, which matches rude and clumsy.
